subject: physics

moments.title: Joule's brewery
moments.body: A wealthy brewer's son, Joule does experiments at his parents' brewery and home laboratory. He measures the mechanical equivalent of heat using a paddle wheel stirring water. 4.18 joules of mechanical work raises the water temperature exactly as 1 calorie of heat would.
moments.takeaway: Heat and mechanical work are forms of the same thing: energy.

moments.title: Mayer's independent derivation
moments.body: A German ship's surgeon notices that venous blood is redder in the tropics than in Europe — bodies need less heat in warm climates. He derives the mechanical equivalent of heat from gas physics. He is ignored, ridiculed, attempts suicide.
moments.takeaway: Independent discovery, rejection, breakdown. Vindication comes late.

moments.title: Helmholtz formalises
moments.body: Helmholtz publishes 'Über die Erhaltung der Kraft' — On the Conservation of Force [Energy]. He shows energy conservation must apply universally if perpetual motion is impossible.
moments.takeaway: Energy conservation becomes a fundamental law of physics.

moments.title: Noether's theorem
moments.body: Noether shows energy conservation is a consequence of time-translation symmetry. The first law of thermodynamics has its deepest explanation.
moments.takeaway: Energy is conserved because the laws of physics don't change in time.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Energy conservation is among the most reliable laws in physics. In general relativity, however, global energy conservation is subtle — energy of cosmological scales is ill-defined.
now.open_questions: Is dark energy 'energy' in the strict sense? Where does it come from?

reflection: Mayer was ignored; Joule was rich; Helmholtz had institutional power. How does class shape who is heard in science?
